purpose: Human-facing editorial patterns for Instagram Reels and TikTok. These rules prioritize retention, story, recognizable musical changes, and visual motivation over mechanical beat matching.
coreRules: Earn attention in the first one to three seconds with the strongest image, result, movement, question, or contrast.
Build one clear setup-tension-payoff arc. A collection of attractive clips is not automatically a story.
Choose a music excerpt with a recognizable entrance, lift, silence, vocal change, chorus, drop, or release that fits the video duration.
Align hero reveals, pacing changes, transition clusters, and endings with large musical changes. Ordinary cuts do not need to land on every beat.
Vary pacing by section: quick hook, readable setup, denser build, longer payoff, concise release or loop.
Use hard cuts by default. Use a transition only when motion, shape, light, location, or a major musical event motivates it.
A major musical wave can motivate a scene change without motivating a transition effect. Require footage compatibility before choosing an effect.
Prefer coherent footage from one person, place, activity, or visual world over maximum source diversity.
Declare the source mode before editing. Stock montages should avoid repeated clips; continuous-footage edits may intentionally reuse one source across distinct time ranges.
Sound design should reinforce selected actions and reveals, not decorate every cut.
Front-load value but preserve a later payoff. Do not hide the only good shot until the final second.

Separate the attention hook from the musical payoff: open with a strong visual or question, use a complete setup phrase to create anticipation, and let the recognizable refrain or drop resolve roughly six to twelve seconds later when the format supports it.
Design multiple opening variants and test retention; small hook changes can matter more than adding effects.

sourceModes.purpose: Demonstrate mood, category coverage, source acquisition, and visual assembly from independently filmed clips.
requirements: review and pin exact source IDs and in-points
keep time of day, palette, subject category, and camera grammar coherent
do not imply one person, route, or location when the footage cannot support that claim

sourceModes.purpose: Demonstrate action continuity, geography, compression of time, and native sound from one recording or session.
requirements: preserve screen direction and readable action
select distinct moments rather than treating low source diversity as a defect
retain or deliberately replace source audio
normalize partial-download timestamps before using the earliest segment

sourceModes.purpose: Demonstrate authored coverage while keeping person, place, activity, wardrobe, light, and sound continuous.
requirements: alternate wide, medium, close detail, POV, and reaction coverage
sync cameras and preserve action matches
use one production sound bed with J-cuts and L-cuts where useful

editStructures.shape: iconic hook, sensory details, movement cluster, hero image, tonal release
motion hook, route context, progression, encounter or acceleration, arrival
preview or question, withheld context, escalating proof, reveal, reaction or release
claim, context, evidence, counterpoint or mistake, takeaway
stakes, setup, attempt, turning point, payoff, reaction or replay
opening motion or question, development, payoff, final frame or sound that reconnects to the opening

majorEvents: final cadence or designed loop point
mapToVisuals: Place the subject or destination reveal on the strongest useful event.
Increase shot density during a build, then hold the payoff longer after the change.
Use one transition cluster or speed change around the major event instead of repeating the same effect.
Use lyric meaning when it creates a clear visual relationship; do not cut across important words only to hit a pulse.
For anticipation edits, label the popular phrase as a payoff rather than an opening hook, preserve the preceding lyric or musical pickup, and increase visual intensity toward it.
Use musical sections rather than a rigid beat grid to shape pacing: readable setup, denser build, longer peak or payoff hold, and relaxed release.
Start and end on complete musical phrases where practical.
avoid: choosing a flat middle section only because it has a stable BPM
cutting every shot to the same number of beats
calling regular pulse alignment a creative success
placing a generic transition on every detected onset

structure: 0-1.5s: strongest destination preview or unusual movement
1.5-6s: two to four details that establish place and person
6-12s: movement sequence that accelerates with the musical build
major music change: hero location, activity, or emotional reveal
final 2-4s: hold, reaction, departure, or frame that can loop
techniques: whip pan only when both clips move in the same direction
brief speed ramp into the reveal

structure: 0-1.5s: close pass, road shape, lean, or destination preview
1.5-5s: start, mirror, controls, or route context
5-12s: continuous movement with enough geography to remain readable
major music change: acceleration, open-road reveal, pass, or destination
ending: arrival, engine stop, dismount, look-back, or POV loop
techniques: speed ramps only around clean acceleration
longer road hold after a fast cluster

structure: 0-1s: iconic crowd, sign, vehicle, or skyline
major music change: wide skyline, crossing, train arrival, or human moment
ending: return to a related opening shape or movement
techniques: one or two motivated zoom or directional transitions
traffic, train, and crowd ambience accents

structure: 0-3s: clear value promise, statement of intent, or question
body: one claim at a time with B-roll mapped to the exact phrase
pattern interrupts: camera change, text, or proof only when attention needs renewal
close: concise takeaway, result, or invitation
techniques: real presenter audio and matching lips

observedExamples.title: Travel Cinematic Short Video | Train Cinematic
observedExamples.observation: The edit uses a restrained opening, a very long train/platform body hold, then a faster final cluster. Its pacing contrast comes from chapters rather than frequent cuts.

observedExamples.title: BMW S1000RR CINEMATIC | 4K
observedExamples.observation: The opening alternates wide, rider, controls, lights, and machine details at high density, then gives moving road shots longer holds. One rider and many shot scales create both coherence and variety.

observedExamples.title: DARJEELING in One Minute | A cinematic Edit
observedExamples.observation: A slow forest and human introduction opens into a landscape reveal, people and place details, then a dense closing montage. The edit changes density by story section.

observedExamples.title: Welcome To Tokyo - Edit | Midnight City
observedExamples.observation: Cuts cluster around large style and musical changes while car, skyline, and headlight motifs are held between clusters. The example supports authored wave maps, not routine beat matching.

reviewRubric: Would the opening stop a cold viewer without relying on a logo or generic title?
Can the viewer describe the subject and promise after three seconds?
Does each shot add new information or emotion?
Does the sequence stay within one believable person, place, or activity?
Is there a visible build and a satisfying payoff?
Do the biggest visual decisions react to the biggest musical decisions?
Are transitions motivated by footage rather than inserted by position?
Does pacing vary enough to create contrast?
Does the ending resolve, invite a replay, or loop cleanly?
Would the edit still make sense with the music muted?
